_doc: Revert-verify mutants for req 9de09856 — the get-body PREDICATE half (the cut position, the raw-output contract, bodyBytes units, and each guard). The WIRING half lives in get-body-9de09856.wiring.spec.json because the driver mutates ONE subject and the registration line sits in program.ts (integration-test-revert-verify §A117). Expectations written BEFORE the run. ⛔ A mutant shifting the cut by +1 was DISCARDED as vacuous before it was written: slice(len+1) eats the separator newline that the following .replace(/^\r?\n/) would have eaten anyway, so both revisions emit identical bytes — the shipped pair is deliberately tolerant of a one-character drift, hence M2 shifts by TWO. ⛤ MIGRATED 2026-09-29 by #4469 (req 2d072437-c19d-49a4-ae89-f20b6185571f): that work item routed get-body's block-end through FrontmatterService.leadingBlock, so four `from` anchors here no longer resolved (spec-anchor-sweep: count 0). Each was re-anchored onto the line that now stands in its place and its `to` re-expressed so the mutant still isolates the SAME guarantee — M8 keeps the cut and only adds the illicit write, M11 drops the last char through the current separator predicate, M12 keeps TypeScript's null-narrowing so it measures the missing diagnostic rather than failing to compile, M13 swaps the guard order while preserving the accessor check. Expectations are unchanged; the driver was re-run to prove they still hold. ⚠ The driver reports SURPLUS redness for M1/M2/M6/M8/M11 (G1b/G3/G4 beyond their `expect`). Those expectations are NOT corrected here, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: **M6 was not touched by the migration at all** and shows the same surplus, so the class pre-dates #4469 — axes G1b/G3/G4 were added to this suite after these expectations were written, and any mutant that changes the printed body reddens them too. Silently widening someone else's `expect` is precisely what integration-test-revert-verify §A44 forbids; reconciling them is this spec's own work item. What #4469 owes is that the MIGRATED mutants still isolate what they always did, and they do: M12/M13 redden exactly ['G12'], M8 still reddens ['G8'], M11 still reddens ['G2','G1b'].
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/get-body.ts

M1_separator_newline_kept._note:
Keeps the newline that separates the frontmatter block from the body, so every body is emitted with a leading 
. G2 compares the raw output byte-for-byte; G1 shows the real cost — set-body writes block + 
 + "
BODY" and reports changed:true, i.e. the round trip stops being a no-op. This is the load-bearing pair.

M2_cut_shifted_by_two._note: Eats the separator newline AND the body's first character. Shifts by two on purpose: see the ⛔ note in _doc — a +1 shift is absorbed by the newline strip and would be a vacuous mutant.

M3_bodybytes_in_utf16_units._note: The set-body floor, mirrored: on the Cyrillic fixture the two measures disagree (every Cyrillic code point is 2 bytes / 1 UTF-16 unit), which is exactly why G4 asserts the byte count AND asserts it differs from .length — without the second assertion the axis would pass under this mutant on ASCII prose.

M4_nonasset_guard_removed._note: Without the guard the non-asset fixture parses fine (it HAS a frontmatter block) and its body is printed — G6 reddens on the printed body and on the missing message. The fixture carries a body precisely so this mutant cannot hide behind the 'no frontmatter block' refusal.

M5_outside_vault_guard_removed._note: The G5 fixture is a VALID asset one level above the vault, so removing the guard makes the read SUCCEED and print a body from outside — the axis reddens on output, not merely on a non-zero exit (§A38: a negated exit-code predicate is satisfied by many outcomes, ENOENT included).

M6_raw_output_extra_newline._note: The most tempting 'harmless' change — println instead of print. It breaks the round trip (set-body appends its own trailing newline, so the body grows by one blank line on every cycle), breaks the byte-exact raw output, and turns the body-less asset's empty output into a newline.

M7_enoent_branch_removed._note: The raw fs error still exits non-zero, so only the MESSAGE distinguishes the two revisions — G7 asserts the message for that reason.

M8_writes_to_the_target.to:
const afterBlock = original.slice(leading.end);
        (await import("fs")).appendFileSync(targetPath, "MUTANT WROTE HERE\n");
M8_writes_to_the_target._note: read-only is a NEGATIVE guarantee — nothing in the shipped code would redden if it silently acquired a write. This mutant supplies the write, so G8 (byte-identical file + unchanged size + surviving stale updatedAt) has a state in which it CAN be red. ⚠ It also perturbs G1/G2/G3/G4 (the file grows before set-body reads it back), which is expected: the driver requires the NAMED axes to be red, not that no others are. ⛔ The first form of this mutant used `require("fs")` and was VACUOUS — the module is ESM, so `require` is not defined, the action threw a ReferenceError inside its own catch and never wrote anything: G1-G4 reddened (the command failed outright) while G8 stayed GREEN, i.e. the mutant measured a crash instead of a write (§A12 — the mutation landed but did not change the behaviour it claimed). The dynamic `import()` form works because the action is already async. Kept in the note so the next author does not re-derive it.

M9_process_exit_restored._note: Restores the truncation defect the review caught: process.exit(0) does not wait for an async stdout write to drain, and stdout is async on a PIPE. Measured on the built bundle with the largest live asset (424 964-byte body): file 424 964 bytes, pipe 65 536 — 84.6 % lost, --json unparseable. Every success axis asserts `exit was never called`, so all of them redden. The DELIVERED-bytes half needs a real process — get-body-9de09856-pipe.harness.ts.

M10_asset_check_reads_whole_file._note: The set-body wording, which tests the WHOLE file: an exo__Asset_uid line in the BODY (yaml fence in docs, template skeleton) then satisfies the guard and a non-asset has its body printed. Live false-positive population is 0 of 46 164, so nothing but this axis can see the hole — which is why it is pinned rather than left as a mirror.

M11_body_last_char_dropped._note: Drops the body's LAST character (M2 shifts the FRONT). ⛤ Note which axes DON'T redden: G1's round trip stays GREEN, because the character lost from a newline-terminated body is exactly the newline set-body appends back — the pair's normalisation MASKS a tail loss. That is precisely why the byte-exact G2 and the no-trailing-newline G1b exist: the load-bearing round-trip axis alone is blind to this class.

M12_no_frontmatter_guard_removed._note: Round-2 review found this branch pinned by NOTHING: every other fixture begins with `---`, so no axis reached it. Without the guard the file falls through to the uid check, which refuses with a DIFFERENT message — hence G12 asserts the message, not merely a non-zero exit (§A38: a negated exit predicate is satisfied by many outcomes).

M13_guard_order_swapped_back._note: Restores the PRE-FIX guard order (whole-file uid check first). The only input that distinguishes the two orders is a file with neither a frontmatter block nor a uid — G12's fixture — where the old order answers 'Not a vault asset' instead of naming the missing block. Both orders refuse and both exit non-zero, so only the MESSAGE separates them: that is why this mutant exists and why G12 asserts the message.
